title: Add database indexes for post.author_id and post.created
description: The post table has no indexes on author_id (FK) or created (the ORDER BY key). Queries do a full table scan plus filesort. Adding indexes (idx_post_created, idx_post_author_id) would improve query performance as the post count grows. Verified finding (assertions.md §4).
notes: Resolved 2026-07-03. Added CREATE INDEX idx_post_created ON post (created DESC) and CREATE INDEX idx_post_author_id ON post (author_id) to flaskr/schema.sql, covering the index.html ORDER BY created DESC listing and the author_id ownership lookups. Verified with a new test tests/test_db.py::test_post_indexes_created that asserts both indexes appear in PRAGMA index_list('post') after init-db. Full suite green: 33 passed (was 32). No migration framework exists and init-db is a destructive re-init, so existing databases pick up the indexes on the next init-db; no separate migration was added (consistent with the current no-migration design).
spec:
1. Add CREATE INDEX idx_post_created ON post (created DESC) to flaskr/schema.sql.
2. Add CREATE INDEX idx_post_author_id ON post (author_id) to flaskr/schema.sql.
3. Verify the index list via PRAGMA index_list('post') after init-db.
4. Verify existing tests still pass after schema change.
5. Consider whether a migration is needed for existing databases (currently no migration framework).
